description: Pale green plates around a white core, warm as a greenhouse. Nobody has found what grows them.
lore: [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]] keeps hers in the apron, left pocket, and has done for longer than most of the people on that meadow have been [[lore/the_waking|awake]]. What is broken re-forms beside the nearest tended fire, and hers is the nearest tended fire for a long way in three directions, so she has had a great deal of practice at the hour afterwards — somebody sitting in the grass with their hands going, short a little of whatever they had been thinking about. She puts the stone into those hands and holds them shut around it until they can manage a cup. Pale green plates around a white middle, warm the way a glasshouse is warm. It does the rest.

Dealers have explained to her, more than once, what she is carrying. That the plates and the white core match nothing anyone has ever broken open. That by every rule of the trade a stone with no shape behind it should not exist. That a collector in the south would pay well for it and ask her nothing. She says that is nice, and thanks them, and goes back to the fire.

Pressed on why she is not curious, she gives the same answer she gives to everything, which is the oldest courtesy there is: you ask a newly woken soul their name and one true thing, and you do not ask where they came from, because for most of them the answer is a hole and the asking widens it. She has never seen why a stone should be handled worse than a person. Seventy-eight gold, forty years, an apron pocket. Her hands are bad in the cold, and it is good for that too.
gm_notes: The warm one, and the deliberate counterweight to the other unbound stones: the impossible object is simply in daily use by the person least interested in it. Solveig's incuriosity is the waking courtesy applied to an object, which is characterisation rather than a dodge — and it leaves the gap open without anybody in the text being unnerved by it. Nothing here is a hint; if the stone ever needs a creature, this record has not spent one.
